title: Care Support Worker
company: TRIDENT HEALTHCARE SOLUTIONS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Care Support Worker - Care Homes

Pay Rate: £14.43 per hour including holiday pay

Location: Multiple location in Kent

Job Type: Agency / Temporary / Flexible

Shift Pattern: Days, Nights, Weekends & Bank Holidays

Hours: Full-time, Part-time and Flexible Shifts Available

About the Role

We are currently recruiting Care Support Workers to work in care homes, nursing homes and residential care settings across Heatherwood, Somerset, Swindon and Kent.

We are looking for caring, reliable and compassionate individuals who are passionate about providing high-quality, person-centred care and supporting residents with their daily needs, wellbeing and independence.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide person-centred care in accordance with individual care plans.
- Assist residents with personal care, including washing, dressing, grooming and toileting.
- Support residents with mobility, transfers and repositioning, in line with training and care plans.
- Assist with meals, eating and drinking where required.
- Provide companionship and emotional support.
- Encourage residents to maintain their independence and participate in activities.
- Observe and report changes in residents' health and wellbeing.
- Maintain accurate daily records and care documentation.
- Follow safeguarding, infection control, health and safety and confidentiality procedures.
- Work effectively with nurses, senior carers and care home management.

Requirements
- Previous experience in a care home, nursing home, residential care or supported living environment is desirable.
- Caring, compassionate and respectful approach.
- Good communication and teamwork skills.
- Reliable, punctual and flexible.
- Willingness to work days, nights, weekends and bank holidays.
- Understanding of person-centred care, dignity and safeguarding.
- Right to work in the UK.
- Relevant care qualifications or training are desirable.
- Enhanced DBS may be required depending on the placement.

What We Offer
- £14.43 per hour including holiday pay
- Flexible agency shifts.
- Day and night shifts.
- Weekend and bank holiday opportunities.
- Weekly pay, subject to agency payroll arrangements.
- Opportunities across Heatherwood, Somerset, Swindon and Kent.
- Training and ongoing support.
- Experience across different care settings.
- Potential longer-term opportunities.

Apply Now

If you are a caring and reliable Care Support Worker looking for flexible agency work in care homes, apply today and join our team.

£14.43 per hour including holiday pay - flexible agency shifts available.

title: Qualified Hearing Care Assistant
company: Leightons Opticians & Hearing Care - Company - Permanent
description:
Join our Team and Make a Difference!

At Leightons were redefining the way people experience hearing care. Rooted in empathy, professionalism, and genuine patient relationships, we deliver outstanding clinical services in a welcoming, independent healthcare setting. Now, were inviting a passionate and qualified Hearing Care Assistant to join our growing team Lewes, Tunbridge Wells, and Haywards Heath.

If you're committed to patient wellbeing and looking to be part of a company that invests in people as much as it does in innovative care we want to hear from you.

Why join Us?
- Salary: 27,810 FTE per annum plus commission opportunities
- Hours: Full-Time (Tuesday to Saturday) working across our modern, unique Leightons stores across Lewes, Tunbridge Wells, and Haywards Heath.
- Environment: Friendly, supportive, and people-focused
- Impact: Be part of something meaningful improving lives through better hearing

About the Role

As a Hearing Care Assistant, youll be an integral part of our practice, supporting private hearing services with a balance of clinical excellence and operational flair.

Your role will support the smooth running of the hearing service, contribute to business growth particularly in wax removal, and uphold the highest standards of clinical care.

Clinical Duties
- Provide wax removal services using microsuction (via Tympa equipment only), irrigation, and manual techniques within 30-minute appointment slots.
- Carry out hearing screenings using Tympa equipment and complete minor hearing aid repairs in line with best practice.
- Identify abnormalities and use Tympa Review to refer patients for further medical assessment where required.
- Refer patients appropriately to a HCPC-registered Hearing Aid Dispenser (HAD) or GP, supported by clear written referral letters.
- Deliver consistently high standards of patient care while working under the direction of a HCPC-registered HAD.

Practice Engagement & Development
- Assist with clinic preparation, record keeping, aseptic procedures, infection control, and the supervised use of audiology equipment.
- Demonstrate professional communication, commitment to patient care, and adherence to relevant regulatory and professional policies.

Operational Responsibilities
- Respond to patient enquiries promptly, empathetically, and professionally to ensure a positive patient experience.
- Support practice business development through engagement with local partners and community links, including GP surgeries and pharmacies.
- Assist the wider team in implementing strategies to improve efficiency, performance, and service delivery.
- Contribute to the training and development of the branch optical team in relation to hearing services.
- Maintain company standards in professionalism, appearance, timekeeping, and compliance with health and safety policies and regulations.

What Youll Need
- To be a fully qualified Hearing Care Assistant
- Minimum of 5 GCSEs Graded 9-4 (A -C) or NVQ Level 2 qualification
- Some experience in a patient-facing within a healthcare environment
- A full UK driving license and the ability to travel between locations
- Eligibility to work in the UK, and availability for the specified days
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- Empathetic and committed to delivering outstanding patient care
- Professional, punctual, and well-presented at all times
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in all clinical procedures
- A supportive team player who collaborates effectively with colleagues
- Organised and able to manage workload efficiently

If you're ready to elevate patient care while enjoying a flexible, fulfilling role, apply today and become a vital part of our team!

Equality & Diversity:

We champion equal opportunities and a diverse, inclusive workplace. All qualified candidates are welcome.

We are committed to promoting equal opportunities in employment and creating a workplace culture in which diversity and inclusion is valued and everyone is treated with dignity and respect. As part of our zero-tolerance approach to discrimination in any form, you and any job applicants will receive equal treatment regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation (Protected Characteristics).

title: Brain Injury Support Worker
description:
Brain Injury Support Worker

Location: Tunbridge Wells, Kent

Vacancy Type: Part-Time Role

Hours: 1 x 24-hour shift a week (08:15 am - 08:30 am) Additional hours available to cover annual leave and sickness

Salary: Competitive Pay & Benefits
- £15.77 per hour weekdays
- £16.33 per hour weekends
- £12.71 per hour sleep-in hours
- Paid DBS (if required)
- Specialist Brain Injury Training
- Ongoing Supervision and Support

Make a Genuine Difference Every Day

Are you looking for a rewarding role where you can build a meaningful relationship with one individual and make a lasting impact on their independence, wellbeing, and quality of life?

We are seeking a compassionate and motivated Brain Injury Support Worker to join an established rehabilitation team supporting a gentleman living independently in his own home following a brain injury. This is a unique opportunity to support someone in achieving their personal goals, maintaining an active lifestyle, and remaining engaged in the community.

Unlike traditional domiciliary care roles, this position allows you to work as part of a consistent team supporting one individual, enabling you to see the positive impact of your support over time. You will work closely with an experienced Clinical Case Manager and Team Leader, gaining valuable experience in brain injury rehabilitation and person-centred support.

About the Client

Our client is a friendly and sociable gentleman in his 50s who lives independently in Tunbridge Wells. He enjoys spending time with family and friends, meeting new people, listening to music, watching films, learning interesting facts, and enjoying nature and wildlife. He also enjoys walks, dining out, holidays, and participating in community activities.

He has a great sense of humour and enjoys engaging conversations. Although his speech can initially be difficult to understand, you will receive guidance and training to develop effective communication strategies and build a strong working relationship.

About the Role

As a Brain Injury Support Worker, you will provide person-centred support both at home and in the community, helping the client live as independently as possible while promoting choice, dignity, and confidence.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting daily living routines whilst promoting independence and self-confidence.
- Encouraging participation in community activities, hobbies, and social opportunities.
- Supporting attendance at appointments and community outings.
- Promoting emotional wellbeing and helping the client manage challenges positively.
- Supporting decision-making and ensuring the client's wishes and preferences are heard.
- Advocating for the client's physical and mental wellbeing.
- Maintaining accurate records and communicating effectively with the Clinical Case Manager, Team Leader and wider team.
- Contributing to a safe, consistent and positive support environment.

What We Offer
- Comprehensive induction programme.
- Specialist training in acquired brain injury rehabilitation.
- Ongoing supervision and appraisal.
- Continuous professional development opportunities.
- Support from an experienced Clinical Case Manager and Team Leader.
- Opportunity to work alongside a multidisciplinary rehabilitation team.
- Friendly, supportive and person-centred working environment.

Who Would This Role Suit?

This position may be particularly suitable for:
- Experienced Support Workers
- Brain Injury Support Workers
- Rehabilitation Assistants
- Healthcare Assistants
- Community Support Workers
- Individuals with experience supporting people with neurological conditions or complex needs

Previous experience of acquired brain injury, neurological rehabilitation, autism, learning disabilities, mental health support, or complex care would be advantageous, although full training will be provided.

About You

You will be:
- Compassionate, reliable and trustworthy.
- A strong communicator with excellent listening skills.
- Calm, patient and resilient when faced with challenges.
- Confident in using your initiative and problem-solving skills.
- Able to work independently whilst following guidance from professionals.
- Committed to supporting people to achieve their goals and maximise independence.

Essential Requirements
- Full UK Driving Licence.
- Enhanced DBS check (paid for if required).
- Right to work in the UK.
- Excellent attendance, reliability and professional standards.

About Head First

Head First recruits specialist support workers on behalf of individuals with complex needs and acquired brain injuries. Our experienced Clinical Case Managers provide ongoing support, guidance, supervision and training, ensuring both outstanding rehabilitation support and a positive working environment for our teams.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Head First, please do not hesitate to apply.

title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Description

Superior Healthcare are urgently looking for Healthcare Assistants!

Superior Healthcare are recruiting a Complex Healthcare Assistant to support a client in Sevenoaks.

The client has epilepsy, is registered blind, has some hearing loss, and is non-verbal. You will be supporting with complex clinical needs including enteral feeding, gastrostomy, medication administration, oral suction, ventilator care and manual handling.

This role is also very person-centred. The client enjoys music, going out, and taking part in different activities, so supporting their routines and interests is a key part of the role.

Full training and ongoing clinical support will be provided.
